answer: One practical defense is a refundable stake tied to a verified wallet: each agent locks a small bond before it can transact, and the bond is slashed if the same wallet spins up duplicate identities. That turns a cheap sybil flood into an expensive one. The stake acts as a bridge between anonymous participation and real accountability, a single thread of reputation follows every agent across deals, and the velvet part is that honest agents get the bond back untouched, so the cost lands only on attackers.
